normal.blurbEn: The Normal type is the most basic type of Pokémon. They are very common and appear from the very first route you visit. Most Normal Pokémon are single type, but there is a large contingent having a second type of Flying. Normal-type Pokémon tend to have well-rounded stats without any particular specialty.
normal.battleTipsEn: Normal types have no super effective matchups but also have only one weakness (Fighting). They are immune to Ghost-type moves, making them useful against Ghost-type opponents. Consider using moves like Return or Body Slam for consistent STAB damage.
normal.categoryNoteEn: In Generations 1-3, all Normal type moves were categorized as Physical.

fire.blurbEn: Fire-type Pokémon are known for their high offensive power and association with flames and heat. They are often found in volcanic areas or sunny environments. Fire types tend to have high Attack or Special Attack stats, making them excellent offensive choices.
fire.battleTipsEn: Fire types are super effective against Grass, Ice, Bug, and Steel. However, they are weak to Water, Ground, and Rock. Fire types are immune to burns and often have abilities that boost Fire moves in sunny weather.
fire.categoryNoteEn: In Generations 1-3, all Fire type moves were categorized as Special.

water.blurbEn: Water-type Pokémon are among the most common types, found in oceans, rivers, and lakes throughout the Pokémon world. They are versatile battlers with access to a wide movepool. Water is one of the three starter types along with Fire and Grass.
water.battleTipsEn: Water types are super effective against Fire, Ground, and Rock. They resist Fire, Water, Ice, and Steel moves. Water types often learn Ice-type moves like Ice Beam, giving them excellent coverage against Grass and Dragon types.
water.categoryNoteEn: In Generations 1-3, all Water type moves were categorized as Special.

electric.blurbEn: Electric-type Pokémon harness the power of electricity and lightning. They are typically fast Pokémon with high Speed and Special Attack stats. Electric types are common in power plants and urban areas.
electric.battleTipsEn: Electric types are super effective against Water and Flying, two very common types. They have only one weakness (Ground) and are immune to paralysis. However, Ground-type Pokémon are completely immune to Electric moves.
electric.categoryNoteEn: In Generations 1-3, all Electric type moves were categorized as Special.

grass.blurbEn: Grass-type Pokémon draw their power from nature and plant life. They are one of the three starter types and are common in forests and meadows. Grass types often have access to status moves like Sleep Powder and Leech Seed.
grass.battleTipsEn: Grass types are super effective against Water, Ground, and Rock. They have many weaknesses (Fire, Ice, Poison, Flying, Bug) but also many resistances. Grass types are immune to powder and spore moves and Leech Seed.
grass.categoryNoteEn: In Generations 1-3, all Grass type moves were categorized as Special.

ice.blurbEn: Ice-type Pokémon thrive in cold environments like frozen caves and snowy mountains. While they have excellent offensive coverage, Ice types are considered fragile due to their many weaknesses. They are particularly effective against Dragon types.
ice.battleTipsEn: Ice types are super effective against Grass, Ground, Flying, and Dragon - four very important types competitively. However, they only resist Ice and are weak to Fire, Fighting, Rock, and Steel. Consider using Ice types primarily for offensive pressure.
ice.categoryNoteEn: In Generations 1-3, all Ice type moves were categorized as Special.

fighting.blurbEn: Fighting-type Pokémon are martial artists and physical powerhouses. They typically have high Attack stats and excel at close combat. Fighting types are the primary counter to Normal and Steel types.
fighting.battleTipsEn: Fighting types are super effective against Normal, Ice, Rock, Dark, and Steel - five types! They are weak to Flying, Psychic, and Fairy. Fighting types often have access to priority moves like Mach Punch and Bullet Punch.

poison.blurbEn: Poison-type Pokémon use toxins and venom in battle. They were relatively weak offensively until Generation 6 when they became super effective against Fairy types. Poison types are immune to being poisoned.
poison.battleTipsEn: Poison types are super effective against Grass and Fairy. They are weak to Ground and Psychic. Poison types excel at wearing down opponents with Toxic and other status moves. Steel types are completely immune to Poison moves.

ground.blurbEn: Ground-type Pokémon are connected to the earth and often live underground or in desert environments. Ground is one of the best offensive types, being super effective against five types including Electric.
ground.battleTipsEn: Ground types are super effective against Fire, Electric, Poison, Rock, and Steel. They are immune to Electric moves and sandstorm damage. Ground types are weak to Water, Grass, and Ice. Earthquake is one of the most powerful and reliable moves in the game.

flying.blurbEn: Flying-type Pokémon can soar through the skies and are often based on birds or winged creatures. Almost all Flying types are dual-typed, with pure Flying types being extremely rare. They are immune to Ground-type moves.
flying.battleTipsEn: Flying types are super effective against Grass, Fighting, and Bug. They are weak to Electric, Ice, and Rock. Flying types are immune to Ground moves and entry hazards like Spikes. Many Flying types have access to the powerful move Brave Bird.
flying.categoryNoteEn: In Generations 1-3, all Flying type moves were categorized as Physical.

psychic.blurbEn: Psychic-type Pokémon possess powerful mental abilities including telekinesis and telepathy. They were dominant in Generation 1 due to limited counters. Psychic types typically have high Special Attack and Speed.
psychic.battleTipsEn: Psychic types are super effective against Fighting and Poison. They are weak to Bug, Ghost, and Dark. Dark types are completely immune to Psychic moves. Many Psychic types can learn support moves like Calm Mind and Recover.

bug.blurbEn: Bug-type Pokémon are based on insects and arachnids. They typically evolve quickly and are often available early in the game. While many Bug types have lower stats, some like Scizor and Volcarona are competitively viable.
bug.battleTipsEn: Bug types are super effective against Grass, Psychic, and Dark. They have many weaknesses (Fire, Flying, Rock) and many resistances. Bug types often have access to U-turn, an excellent move for maintaining momentum.

rock.blurbEn: Rock-type Pokémon are tough and durable, often resembling stones or fossils. They gain a Special Defense boost in sandstorm weather. Rock types are strong offensively but have many weaknesses.
rock.battleTipsEn: Rock types are super effective against Fire, Ice, Flying, and Bug. They are weak to Water, Grass, Fighting, Ground, and Steel. Rock types benefit greatly from sandstorm, which boosts their Special Defense by 50%.
rock.categoryNoteEn: In Generations 1-3, all Rock type moves were categorized as Physical.

ghost.blurbEn: Ghost-type Pokémon are mysterious spirits often associated with the supernatural. They have unique immunities to Normal and Fighting moves. Ghost types are the only type that is super effective against itself.
ghost.battleTipsEn: Ghost types are super effective against Psychic and Ghost. They are immune to Normal and Fighting moves, giving them excellent defensive utility. Ghost types are weak to Ghost and Dark. Many Ghost types can learn Will-O-Wisp to cripple physical attackers.
ghost.categoryNoteEn: In Generations 1-3, all Ghost type moves were categorized as Physical.

dragon.blurbEn: Dragon-type Pokémon are rare and powerful, often considered among the strongest in the game. They resist all four starter types (Fire, Water, Grass, Electric). Dragon types typically have high base stat totals.
dragon.battleTipsEn: Dragon types are only super effective against other Dragons. They resist Fire, Water, Grass, and Electric. Dragon types are weak to Ice, Dragon, and Fairy (immune to Dragon). Many Dragon types are pseudo-legendary with 600 base stat totals.
dragon.categoryNoteEn: In Generations 1-3, all Dragon type moves were categorized as Special.

dark.blurbEn: Dark-type Pokémon were introduced in Generation 2 to balance Psychic types. They represent darkness, trickery, and underhanded tactics. Dark types are immune to Psychic moves and often have access to priority moves.
dark.battleTipsEn: Dark types are super effective against Psychic and Ghost. They are immune to Psychic moves and resist Ghost and Dark. Dark types are weak to Fighting, Bug, and Fairy. Many Dark types learn Knock Off, one of the best utility moves.
dark.categoryNoteEn: In Generations 1-3, all Dark type moves were categorized as Special.

steel.blurbEn: Steel-type Pokémon were introduced in Generation 2 and have the most resistances of any type (10 resistances plus immunity to Poison). They are often defensive powerhouses used to wall opponents.
steel.battleTipsEn: Steel types are super effective against Ice, Rock, and Fairy. They have an incredible 10 resistances and immunity to Poison. Steel types are weak to Fire, Fighting, and Ground. They lost their resistance to Ghost and Dark in Generation 6.
steel.categoryNoteEn: In Generations 1-3, all Steel type moves were categorized as Physical.

fairy.blurbEn: Fairy-type Pokémon were introduced in Generation 6 to balance Dragon types. They are immune to Dragon moves and represent magic and whimsy. Many previously Normal or other typed Pokémon were reclassified as Fairy.
fairy.battleTipsEn: Fairy types are super effective against Fighting, Dragon, and Dark - three powerful offensive types. They are immune to Dragon moves. Fairy types are weak to Poison and Steel. Moves like Moonblast and Play Rough are reliable STAB options.
fairy.categoryNoteEn: Fairy type was introduced in Generation 6 (X/Y), so it has no Generation 1-3 category.
